title: Curvilinear Optical Proximity Correction via Cardinal Spline
problem: Optical proximity correction (OPC) must handle curvilinear mask patterns with complex geometry; traditional OPC approaches struggle with curvature while maintaining mask rule checking compliance.
motivation: Advanced lithography requires precise optical proximity correction; curvilinear mask patterns enable better pattern fidelity but complicate OPC.
method: Proposes curvilinear OPC framework using cardinal splines to represent mask patterns through control points; iteratively adjusts control points guided by lithography simulation; develops comprehensive MRC checking methods for width, space, area, and curvature; designs algorithms to fit inverse lithography technique (ILT) results and resolve MRC violations.
key_novelty: Cardinal spline-based curvilinear mask representation for OPC optimization with integrated MRC compliance.
contributions: Cardinal spline representation of mask patterns enabling smooth curvature handling
Comprehensive MRC checking methods for width, space, area, and curvature constraints
Algorithms for fitting ILT results and resolving MRC violations
Demonstrated effectiveness as viable OPC/ILT alternative

metrics.other: MRC compliance; pattern fidelity vs ILT results

limitations: Not discussed—focus on methodology without performance metrics or scalability analysis.
primary_theme: Cardinal spline-based curvilinear OPC with MRC compliance
